% ---- derivatives
\cssec{Gradient and Hessian}
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{Gradient} $\nabla f = \big(\tfrac{\partial f}{\partial x_1}, \dots, \tfrac{\partial f}{\partial x_n}\big)^\top$ points in the direction of steepest ascent and is perpendicular to level sets. Lecture example $f = \val{ex.lecture.tex.f}$: $\nabla f\val{ex.lecture.point} = \val{ex.lecture.grad}$.
  \item \textbf{Hessian} $H = \big[\tfrac{\partial^2 f}{\partial x_i\,\partial x_j}\big]$ is symmetric when the second partials are continuous (Schwarz). Lecture: $H_{11} = \val{ex.lecture.tex.h11}$, $H_{12} = \val{ex.lecture.tex.h12}$, $H_{22} = \val{ex.lecture.tex.h22}$, $\det H\val{ex.lecture.point} = \val{ex.lecture.det}$. A quadratic has a constant $H$.
  \item \textbf{Hessian of a polynomial}: a square $c\,x_i^2$ gives $H_{ii} = 2c$; a cross term $c\,x_ix_j$ gives $H_{ij} = H_{ji} = c$; variables that never meet give $0$.
  \item \textbf{Directional derivative} $\tfrac{\partial f}{\partial s}(x) = \lim_{\alpha \to 0^+} \tfrac{f(x + \alpha s) - f(x)}{\alpha} = s^\top \nabla f(x)$, a rate per unit of $\alpha$. D2: $s = \val{ex.dir.s}$, $\nabla f = \val{ex.dir.grad}$, $s^\top \nabla f = \val{ex.dir.value}$; per unit length $\val{ex.dir.tex.perLength}$; steepest descent $-\|\nabla f\| = \val{ex.dir.tex.steepest}$.
\end{itemize}

% ---- taylor
\cssec{Taylor's formula}
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{Taylor}: $f(x + h) = f(x) + \nabla f(x)^\top h + \tfrac12\, h^\top H(x)\, h + o(\|h\|^2)$. The linear term changes sign with $h$, the quadratic term does not.
  \item $h^\top H h = H_{11}h_1^2 + 2H_{12}h_1h_2 + H_{22}h_2^2$: for the lecture $H\val{ex.lecture.point}$ and $h = \val{ex.lecture.h}$ it is $\val{ex.lecture.hHh}$.
  \item \textbf{Accuracy}: from $\val{ex.lecture.point}$ along $t\,\val{ex.lecture.h}$ with $t = \val{ex.taylor.tenth.t}$ the linear model $\val{ex.taylor.tex.lin}$ is off by $\val{ex.taylor.tenth.tex.errLin}$, the quadratic $\val{ex.taylor.tex.quad}$ by $\val{ex.taylor.tenth.tex.errQuad}$.
  \item \textbf{Quadratic} $f$: the formula is exact. $q = \val{ex.quad.tex.f}$, $x = \val{ex.quad.point}$, $h = \val{ex.quad.h}$ give $\val{ex.quad.value}$ both ways.
\end{itemize}

% ---- definiteness
\cssec{Definiteness}
\begin{itemize}
  \item Symmetric $A$: $A \succ 0$ if $h^\top A h > 0$ for all $h \ne 0$ (a bowl); $A \succeq 0$ if $h^\top A h \ge 0$ (a bowl or a trough); $A \prec 0$, $A \preceq 0$ likewise (a dome); \textbf{indefinite} if $h^\top A h$ takes both signs (a saddle).
  \item \textbf{Eigenvalues decide}: all $> 0$, all $\ge 0$ or mixed signs. For $2 \times 2$: $\lambda^2 - (A_{11} + A_{22})\lambda + \det A = 0$. A1: $\val{ex.eig.pd.tex.poly} = 0$, $\lambda = \val{ex.eig.pd.values}$; C2: $\val{ex.eig.indef.tex.poly} = 0$, $\lambda = \val{ex.eig.indef.values}$.
  \item \textbf{Sylvester}: $A \succ 0 \iff \Delta_k > 0$ for all $k$; $A \prec 0 \iff (-1)^k \Delta_k > 0$ for all $k$. A3: $\Delta = \val{ex.syl.minors}$, so $H \succ 0$.
  \item \textbf{Semidefinite}: leading minors cannot tell. Use \textbf{all} principal minors ($\val{ex.syl.nPrincipal}$ of them for $\val{ex.syl.nLeading} \times \val{ex.syl.nLeading}$) or eigenvalues with a tolerance.
\end{itemize}

% ---- minima
\cssec{Minima and feasible directions}
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{Local minimum} $x^* \in \Omega$: for some $\varepsilon > 0$, $f(x) \ge f(x^*)$ for all $x \in \Omega$ with $\|x - x^*\| < \varepsilon$. \textbf{Global}: for all $x \in \Omega$. \textbf{Strict}: $f(x) > f(x^*)$ for $x \ne x^*$.
  \item \textbf{Interior point}: a small ball around it lies in $\Omega$; otherwise a \textbf{boundary} point. Quadrant $x \ge 0$: $\val{ex.quadrant.interior}$ is interior, $\val{ex.quadrant.boundary}$ is on the boundary.
  \item \textbf{Feasible direction} $s \ne 0$ at $x$: $x + \alpha s \in \Omega$ for all $\alpha \in [0, \alpha_0]$ with some $\alpha_0 > 0$. D1 at $\val{ex.quadrant.boundary}$: $s_1 \ge 0$; at the corner $\val{ex.quadrant.corner}$: $s \ge 0$; at an interior point: every $s$.
\end{itemize}

% ---- conditions
\cssec{Optimality conditions}
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{First order, necessary}: $s^\top \nabla f(x^*) \ge 0$ for every feasible $s$; at an interior point this is $\nabla f(x^*) = 0$, a \textbf{stationary point}. One violating direction rejects a point (D1); accepting needs all of them.
  \item \textbf{Second order, necessary} (interior point): $\nabla f(x^*) = 0$ and $H(x^*) \succeq 0$.
  \item \textbf{Sufficient} (interior point): $\nabla f(x^*) = 0$ and $H(x^*) \succ 0$ give a strict local minimum. There is \textbf{no} sufficient condition of first order.
  \item \textbf{Procedure}: solve $\nabla f = 0$; at each candidate $H \succ 0$ means a minimum, $H \prec 0$ a maximum, indefinite $H$ a saddle, singular semidefinite $H$: analyse $f$ directly. Call a minimum \textbf{global} only by convexity or a bound.
\end{itemize}

% ---- gap
\cssec{When the second-order test is silent}
\begin{itemize}
  \item Same data, opposite answers: $f_1 = \val{ex.gap.tex.f1}$ and $f_2 = \val{ex.gap.tex.f2}$ both have $\nabla f(0) = 0$ and $H(0) = 0$; $f_1$ has a strict global minimum at $0$ (B4), $f_2$ no extremum (B3).
  \item \textbf{Bound from below}: $f_1 \ge 0 = f_1(0)$. \textbf{Restrict to a line}: $f_2(x_1, 0) = x_1^3$ changes sign. \textbf{Polar form}: $f_2 = \val{ex.monkey.tex.polar}$, \val{ex.monkey.nSectors} sectors of $\val{ex.monkey.sectorDeg}^\circ$. A picture is a guide, not a proof.
  \item \textbf{Flat directions}: $x_1^2$ has a whole line of non-strict minima with $H = \operatorname{diag}(2, 0)$; $x_1^3 + x_2^2$ has $H(0) \succeq 0$ and no extremum (H1).
\end{itemize}

% ---- convexity
\cssec{Convexity}
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{Convex set}: $\lambda x + (1 - \lambda) y \in \Omega$ for all $x, y \in \Omega$, $\lambda \in [0, 1]$. \textbf{Convex function}: $f\big(\lambda x + (1 - \lambda) y\big) \le \lambda f(x) + (1 - \lambda) f(y)$ for all such $x$, $y$, $\lambda$. Every norm ball is convex (C1); a ring is not.
  \item \textbf{Test} ($f \in C^2$, open convex $\Omega$): convex $\iff H(x) \succeq 0$ everywhere; $H \succ 0$ everywhere gives strict convexity. C2: $x_1^2 + x_2^2 + a\,x_1x_2$ has $\lambda = 2 \pm a$ and is convex $\iff |a| \le \val{ex.family.bound}$.
  \item \textbf{Local is global}: for a convex $f$ on a convex $\Omega$ every local minimum is global, and on $\mathbb R^n$ the condition $\nabla f(x^*) = 0$ becomes sufficient.
  \item \textbf{Least squares} $L(w) = \tfrac1m \|Xw - y\|^2$: $H_L = \tfrac2m X^\top X \succeq 0$, so every solution of $X^\top X w = X^\top y$ is a global minimizer. Line fit: $w^* = \val{ex.fit.tex.w}$.
\end{itemize}

% ---- traps
\cssec{Top traps}
\begin{itemize}
  \item A cross term $c\,x_ix_j$ gives $H_{ij} = H_{ji} = c$: not $c/2$ (the entry of $A$ in $x^\top A x$) and not $2c$ (only squares double).
  \item Leading minors decide only strict definiteness: $\operatorname{diag}(0, -1)$ and $\operatorname{diag}(0, 1)$ both have $\Delta_1 = \Delta_2 = 0$, yet one is $\preceq 0$ and the other $\succeq 0$.
  \item Gradient first: $H \succ 0$ at a non-stationary point proves nothing. A2: $H\val{ex.classify.notStationary.point} \succ 0$, but $\nabla f = \val{ex.classify.notStationary.grad}$.
  \item $s^\top \nabla f$ is a rate per unit of $\alpha$: compare directions only after dividing by $\|s\|$.
  \item In code a saddle needs \texttt{w.min() < -tol and w.max() > tol}; the chained \texttt{w.min() < -tol < w.max()} calls $\operatorname{diag}(0, -1)$ a saddle.
\end{itemize}
